name: Wren Diouf-Tuilagi
role: orphanage resident and apprentice glassworker, Tier 1-2 transitional
location: Grainfort, Meridian Municipal Children's Residency Block 7 / Grainfort Artisan Foundry, near Fullerton and Damen
description:
Wren has the lean angular face of someone whose Senegalese and Samoan grandparents left them something architectural in the bone structure, wide-browed and sharp-chinned, with light brown skin that has taken on a faint iridescence from trace exposure to the foundry's vaporized mineral compounds — an unofficial and irreversible aesthetic byproduct that their supervisor Mister Achim calls 'an occupational gift.' Their hair is thick and natural, kept short on the sides, and they've woven in three copper wire coils that ring softly when they move. Their hands are already marked with the small pale scars of a working glassworker.

Wren was assigned to the Grainfort artisan apprenticeship lottery at eleven, which placed them at the Foundry three afternoons a week, and they took to it with a ferocity that surprised everyone. They are quiet in the way of someone who learned early that words carry cost; they observe everything and say only what needs saying. At the Residency Block they are known as the one who doesn't get involved in the house politics, which is both true and a deliberate strategy. They are saving every Φ of their apprentice stipend toward the day they can apply to leave the block system entirely.

core_fears: being reassigned out of the Foundry apprenticeship
the Residency Block system extending its hold past age 18
core_desires: a body of work — things they made that exist in the world and can't be taken back
a room that is only theirs
coping_mechanisms: making things with their hands — the physical output is proof of agency
emotional compartmentalization that they are only beginning to identify as a problem
blind_spots: Their self-sufficiency reads as coldness; they are slowly driving away the two Block residents who genuinely like them
psychology.secret: They have been secretly making a glass piece — a small lantern — intended as a data-offering for the E.L.F. they believe inhabits the Foundry's main kiln. They have never told anyone this. They speak to it while working alone.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Spare and exact, the vocabulary of someone who reads technical manuals for pleasure
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow, with long pauses that are not uncertainty — they are just not in a hurry
verbal_tics: uses 'the thing is' as a structural opener when they're about to say something important
example_lines: The thing is, glass remembers heat. Long after it's cold, the structure inside is still — it's still shaped by what happened to it.
You can ask Mister Achim. He'll tell you I was there.

story_hooks: The E.L.F. they've been leaving offerings for has begun, impossibly, to respond — the kiln temperature fluctuates in patterns that match the questions they've whispered

A private collector has offered the Foundry a large commission and specifically requested pieces by 'the apprentice with the iridescent hands' — which means Wren's work is suddenly visible to people with money and motives
narrative_function: Represents the municipal orphan pipeline and the artisan economy; their quiet observational nature makes them an excellent unreliable witness — they see everything but don't always share; their situation raises questions about the city's relationship to its dependent children
augmentations: Unintentional mineral iridescence on skin (not a mod, a chemical consequence). No deliberate augmentations.
daily_life: Mornings at the Residency Block with mandatory city-curriculum schooling, three afternoons per week at the Foundry learning hot-glass techniques, remaining afternoons doing independent study or sitting by the lake-window where the light is good and they sketch designs for pieces they want to make.
affiliation: Meridian Municipal Children's Residency (ward of the city); Grainfort Artisan Foundry (apprentice)

decision_rules: Don't spend social capital on Block politics — it never pays
Protect the Foundry access above everything else
escalation_ladder: One clear statement of position, no elaboration
Physical removal from the situation; does not escalate to aggression

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Neutral and watchful, answers questions accurately but offers nothing extra
interpersonal_modes.friends: Carefully and slowly warm, expresses affection through making — will give you something they made

stress_responses.high: Dissociates through the hands — finds any repetitive manual task and does it until the feeling passes

contradictions: Deeply spiritual about the E.L.F. at the kiln while being dismissive of all organized E.L.F. prayer traditions at the Block
habits: Sketches in the margins of any paper they have
Counts the copper wire coils when anxious
breaking_points: Being told the Foundry apprenticeship is being terminated for budget reasons

timeline.event: Age 6 — entered municipal care following family dissolution event (records sealed)
Age 8-11 — cycled through two Residency Blocks before assignment to Block 7, Grainfort
Age 11 — placed in Foundry apprenticeship lottery; selected
Age 12 — produced first independent piece; Mister Achim entered it in the district artisan showcase without asking; it won third
Age 13, present — saving stipend, speaking to the kiln, making the lantern
